alex_chen: Heads-up — the latency dashboard for /v1/embeddings is showing p99 < p95 on the endpoint breakdown. Is this a visualization bug or are we folding different sample sources together?
benjamin_lee: huh that's wild. can you paste a screenshot?
sophie_ng: I saw something similar last week when we merged client-side and server-side traces into the same rollup. mixing sample origins + different histo buckets can invert quantiles.
alex_chen: screenshot: <link> — it’s specifically in the per-endpoint view, p50=120ms, p95=300ms, p99=250ms.
maria_garcia: that pattern screams mixed aggregation sources. if some requests come from uninstrumented clients, server-only events shift tails differently. do we show sample_count anywhere?
sophie_ng: we do, but it's hidden under the legend. proposal: surface "sample origin" and show sample_count per percentile line. Also add an aggregation-mode tag (client|server|combined) on the series.
benjamin_lee: agreed. short-term: can you run a quick grouped query to confirm? example:
```sql
SELECT
  quantile(0.5, latency_ms) as p50,
  quantile(0.95, latency_ms) as p95,
  quantile(0.99, latency_ms) as p99,
  count() as samples,
  source
FROM traces
WHERE route = '/v1/embeddings'
GROUP BY source
```
benjamin_lee: if different 'source' groups have small counts, the merged quantile lines can look wrong.
ops-bot: deploy 2025-06-01T20:12Z: rollout dashboard/latency-widget v2 -> canary (10%) :rocket:
alex_chen: fwiw, on my local run the per-source groups show p99 larger than p95 per-group. the inversion only appears after the rollup blend.
sophie_ng: that's expected: combining two distributions and then computing quantiles is not the same as computing quantiles per-group and then merging. tdigest rollups can help but only if the upstream encodes origin metadata.
maria_garcia: long-term UX idea: add a toggle "blend by default" with a tooltip explaining the semantics + show a diff button "compare blended vs per-source". that'd catch this quickly for PMs.
benjamin_lee: engineering work: (1) surface sample origin in the legend, (2) add sample_count badge, (3) Make blended series visually distinct and add an inline hint when counts are low. low-risk patch, I can take the backend bits.
sophie_ng: backend note: when sample_count < 200 for any source, show a warning banner: "Low sample sizes may invert percentiles when blended."
alex_chen: can we also make the API expose aggregation_mode so the console can request pre-merged vs per-source timeseries? product wants a single series by default but with an obvious toggle.
maria_garcia: yep, that's the plan. i'll draft the UX copy.
benjamin_lee: i'll open a PR for the telemetry API and the sample_count telemetry flag. assigning to @sophie_ng for tdigest integration review.
sophie_ng: thanks — will review. once merged we should run a smoke on the embeddings endpoint and post results here. :thumbsup:
alex_chen: awesome. thanks everyone — feel better knowing this is an explainable aggregation artifact, not a network issue.
ops-bot: alert: latency-dashboard-warning created for /v1/embeddings — rule: blended-quantile-inversion (silence: 1h)
